title: Lemon posset
summary: Three ingredients: cream boiled with sweetener, then set by nothing more than lemon juice into something silky and sharp.
steps: Put the cream, allulose and zest in a wide saucepan and bring slowly to the boil, stirring until the allulose dissolves.
Let it boil gently for 3 minutes, watching that it does not rise over the rim. This reduction is what gives the posset its body.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the lemon juice. Leave it to stand for 10 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve into a jug to remove the zest, then pour into six small ramekins or glasses.
Cool, then refrigerate uncovered for at least 5 hours, until set.
dairy_free_notes: Coconut cream does not thicken with acid the way dairy cream does, so it relies on chilling to set and will be softer and spoonable rather than firm; simmer it a little longer and chill overnight.
tips: Allulose rather than erythritol keeps the posset smooth: erythritol tends to recrystallise in a cold cream.

origin.history: In medieval and Tudor England a posset was a hot drink of milk or cream curdled with wine or ale, often spiced and taken as a remedy. The modern lemon posset, a set cream thickened by citrus juice, is a much later descendant that became a popular British dessert in the twentieth century.
